sentences.text:
This petition is filed by the L.R's of one deceased Kotte Vijay Kumar under Section 166 of M.V.Act,
1989 seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- in respect of his death in Road Traffic Accident.
2. It is stated in the petition that, 1 st petitioner is the wife, 2nd petitioner is daughter, 3rd petitioner is the son of deceased.

That on 03.06.2023 at about 4.00 pm one Kotte Vijay Kumar was traveling in Ashoka Leyland Dost vehicle bearing No.AP-39-U- 1171 at Kondareddy cross, Madanapalli, Tirupati NH-71 Road and the driver of the said lorry drove the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the KSRTC bus bearing reg.No.KA-40-F-1143 and caused accident.

Due to said impact, Kotte Vijay Kumar fell down and sustained blood stained injuries all over the body and he was taken to nearby by Piler Govt.hospital, the duty doctor examined him and declared brought dead.
Postmortem was conducted and dead body was handed over to his family members.
Petitioners have spent more (SCCH-12) 3 MVC No.4729/2023 than Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and for performing the last rites.
3. Prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was working as a Mason and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
That deceased was the only earning member in the family due to his untimely death petitioners are put to great agony, pain and deep mental stress and facing financial hardship.
The accident is due to rash and negligent driving of driver of bearing No.AP- 39-U-1171.
The complaint has been lodged in Piler Police Station in Cr.No.146/2023 under Section 279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC against the rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing no.AP-39-U-1171.
The 1st and 2nd respondents are insurer and owner of vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioners.
On all these grounds petitioners prayed to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with costs and interest in the above case.
4. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 and 2 are served.
They appeared before this court through their respective counsel and filed separate written statement.
5. 1st respondent insurance company in its written statement contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
That Sec.134 (C) and Sec.158(6) of MV Act is not complied.

It has issuance of policy of insurance in favour of 2 nd respondent in respect of Ashoka Leyland Dost bearing reg.No.AP-39-U-1171, the liability of it is limited to therms and conditions of policy and subject to valid and effective driving license and subject to confirmation of 64 VB of Insurance Act,
1938.
It has denied the involvement of vehicle in the alleged (SCCH-12) 4 MVC No.4729/2023 accident.
That deceased was traveling as gratuitous passenger in goods vehicle which is in contravention with the policy terms and conditions whose risk is not required to be covered under the statute.

Further the claim petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties as it emanates from the records that the alleged accident and death/injury is entirely due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing reg. No.KA-40F-1143.

That he was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident and further was not qualified for holding or obtaining such driving license and further not satisfied the requirements of the Rule 3 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.
The owner of the vehicle willfully entrusted the vehicle to the said driver, thereby the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.

He denied the age, occupation, income of the deceased.
He also denied the accident.

That on the alleged date of accident his Ashoka Leyland Dost bearing reg.No.AP-39-U-1171 was driven by its driver by name S.Mohammed Irshad, S/o S.Mubarak Basha on the extreme left side of Madanapalli-Tirupati NH-71 road slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations while so proceeding reached at Kondareddy cross, Piler Town and Mandal, Annamayya District, Andhra Pradesh, at that time, (SCCH-12) 5 MVC No.4729/2023 suddenly the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing reg.No.KA-40-F-1143 came in rash and negligent manner endangering to human life, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations, he himself dashed to his Lorry.
That he is the R.C owner of Ashoka Leyland Dost bearing reg.No.AP-39-U-1171 and the RTO and such other documents are standing in his name.

The same was insured with 1st respondent New India Assurance Company ltd vide policy No.61270631220100001158, valid from 19.03.2023 to 18.03.2024, the policy was in force as on the date of accident, the driver by name S.Mohammad Irshad who drove the 1st respondent vehicle also possess valid and effective driving licence vide DL No.AP40320130000738, valid from 04.03.2022 to 09.12.2033.
On all these grounds 2nd respondent prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
7. On application filed by 1st respondent KSRTC is also impleaded as 3rd respondent and it has appeared through counsel.

It has filed written statement contending that on the date and time of alleged accident, the bus in question was on its schedule trip from Tirupathi to Bagepallu and was being driven by its driver slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules and while it was so proceeding at Kodandarama circle in Piller town, at that time, the Ashok Leyland Goods vehicle bearing no.AP-39-U-1171 came form opposite side being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner with terrific and in order to overtake a vehicle proceeding ahead of him came to the extreme right side by crossing the midpoint and due to over speed lost control over the vehicle and dashed to the bus and caused accident.
That (SCCH-12) 6 MVC No.4729/2023 the driver of the aforesaid vehicle was wholly responsible but the driver of KRTC bus was no way responsible.
That it is not a necessary party but it has been implicated for oblique reasons.

As such,
petition against this respondent is liable to be dismissed.
Age, occupation, income and other averments are denied.
On all these grounds 3rd respondent prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

14. On perusal of those documents it can be noticed that wife of the deceased has given first information to the police on the same of the incident stating that her husband is working as (SCCH-12) 8 MVC No.4729/2023 Hamali in Piller town with one Mohammed Ershad.

sentences.text: That due to accident Ershad died on the spot and her husband also sustained grievous injuries.

That she went to the spot along with relatives in neighbor's auto to the spot of accident and her husband is found to be sustained grievous injuries, he was taken to hospital in ambulance, but doctor after examining him declared as dead.
That the driver of luggage vehicle was negligent and action may be taken against him.
15. In the first information there is no mention about negligence of the KSRTC bus driver.
As per the P.M. report Vijay Kumar died due to head injury.
The accident has taken place on the right side of the cross road.
On which side bus was coming and from which side lorry was moving is not shown in the rough sketch.
But as per the final report, luggage vehicle driver was found to be negligent.
But since he died in the accident, abated charge sheet is filed against him.
16. The owner of the luggage vehicle has filed written statement stating his driver was not negligent but KSRTC bus driver was negligent.
Similarly, KSRTC filed written statement that its driver was not negligent, but luggage vehicle driver was negligent.
Both owner and KSRTC have not led any evidence in (SCCH-12) 9 MVC No.4729/2023 support of their written statement contentions.
Therefore, both of their version is not backed by supportive evidence from their side.
Therefore case has to be decided on the basis of available documents on record.
17. 1st respondent insurance company denied the negligence of its insured vehicle driver and also contended that deceased was gratuitous passenger on goods vehicle.
On that ground it has denied it liability.
In first information itself it is mentioned that deceased was hamali at Ashok Leyland luggage vehicle.
The owner has not disputed the same.
Though suggestions are made to P.W.1 that deceased was not laborer, and he was gratuitous passenger
,the said suggestion is denied.
There is first information to show that, he was hamali, but there is no other contrary document to show he was not laborer in luggage vehicle authorized by the owner of the goods.
Therefore, he cannot be considered as gratitious passenger in the goods vehicle.
Therefore on the basis of oral and documentary evidence, petitioners have proved this issue in their favour.
Accordingly, I hold in the affirmative.
18. ISSUE NO.2 : To prove the age of the deceased petitioners have produced aadhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P.11.
It shows that he was born in the year 1971.
As on the date of accident i.e.,03.06.2023 deceased was aged 52 years.
19. In the petition it is mentioned that he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month by doing Mason work.
To prove his occupation and income no document is produced.
Hence, notional income has to be considered.
Accident having taken (SCCH-12) 10 MVC No.4729/2023 place in 2023, the notional income of deceased is considered as Rs.16,000/-.
In the petition it is stated that all the petitioners were dependents upon the deceased.
They are wife and children.
Their separate income is not proved.
Therefore all of them are considered as dependents for the purpose of grant of compensation.
Accordingly, this issue is held partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
In view of above reasons petitioners are entitled for compensation.
In view of valid insurance policy, respondent no.1 shall indemnify the insured and shall be directed to deposit the entire compensation amount.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under;
21. Loss of dependency :
As per the Praney Sethi case future prospects of the deceased will have to be added to the monthly income.
In case of self employed 10% of the income has to be added to the monthly income to the age group between 50-60 years.
Age of the deceased in this case is 52 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, monthly income of deceased is Rs.16,000/- + 1,600/- = Rs.17,600/-.
Further deceased being married having 3 dependents 1/3rd of his income shall be deducted towards his personal expenses.
As such, loss of dependency of the petitioners due to the death of their family member is Rs.15,48,888/-.
22. Loss of love and affection:
Petitioners being L.R's of the deceased have lost the love and affection of their family member.
Therefore, for loss of love and affection compensation has to be granted.

There is no hard and fast rule in respect of measuring love and affection but, in the opinion of this court if amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded for loss of love and affection, the interest of justice would be met.
Accordingly, amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded.
23. Loss of Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses:

As per the judgment in Praney Sethi's case, the quantum of compensation for Loss of Consortium is fixed @ Rs.40,000/- and loss of estate and funeral expenses is fixed @ Rs.15,000/- respectively and it is revisable at 10% every 3 years.

As such, accident having taken place in the year 2023, under the head of loss of estate Rs.16,500/-, for funeral expenses Rs.16,500/- and for loss of consortium Rs.44,000/- each to petitioner No.1 to 3 is awarded.

Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation as under:
Sl.No. Particulars of Heads Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Dependency : Rs.15,48,888/-
2. Loss of love & affection : 50,000/-
3. Loss of Consortium to : 1,32,000/-
petitioner No.1 to 3 ( Rs.44,000/- each)
4. Loss of estate : 16,500/-

Therefore, I hold that the petitioners are entitled for a compensation of Rs.17,63,888/- from 1st respondent insurance company, in view of valid insurance policy as on the date of accident.
Hence, I answer this Issue in "Partly in the Affirmative".
24. ISSUE No.4: Petitioners have sought for compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- in respect of death of Vijay Kumar in road traffic accident.
As per the settled law, the interest that could be awarded on the compensation is only 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till the payment.
They being L.Rs of the deceased are entitled for compensation in the apportionment of 70:15:15.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

It is held that, petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.17,63,888/- with interest @ 6%
p.a. on the said amount from the date of petition till the date of payment.

In view of valid insurance policy, respondent no.1 shall indemnify the insured and hereby directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with (SCCH-12) 13 MVC No.4729/2023 interest before this court within 2 months from the date of this order.

In such apportionment entire compensation awarded to petitioner no.
2 and 3 shall be released in their favour without making F.D and 50% of compensation awarded to 1st petitioner wife shall be kept in F.D in her name in any nationalized bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 50% shall be released in her favour. .
The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.

p.a. on the said amount from the date of petition till the date of payment.
